writeup: TIC 40100356 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.5139 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing a 1.79% dimming of the star's light, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 72.1 using the Box Least Squares method. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 22.6, though the centroid offset measures 3.3 arcseconds from the nominal target position. No secondary eclipse was detected in the data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it potentially new to the scientific record. The automated pipeline's machine-learning classifier assigned it a score of 0.26 on its likelihood scale, and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
